The models can predict the next amino acid if given the start of little-studied bacterial proteins. No other model tested can do this, and the models fail to predict the sequence if the protein is shuffled. Fable 5.2 beats every open protein language model tested.

The study's findings suggest that while current models can identify common alignment evaluations, making them less detectable can refine their efficacy.

articles.headline: World 2030
articles.blurb: Predicting how AI will affect the economy requires looking at all of the different components of that economy and figuring out how they might affect each other. World 2030 is a study that sets up nine groups (AI labs, big employers, banks and insurers, utilities, startups, universities, workers, governments, and the Fed) and runs the US economy forward in six-month turns to 2030. It aimed to identify both the invariants and the boundaries of what can change as these powerful forces interact with each other. The study predicts that AI will break per-seat software pricing and cut US junior desk hiring.

articles.headline: d1.2: State-of-the-Art Omnimodal Decision Models

They can also read a value from the input, find every passage of a kind in a text, locate things in a picture, estimate a number, and pick every option that applies. d1.2-ultra ranks first among decision models on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index v2.1. Both models are available on the Liquid API at $0.02 per million input tokens for d1.2 and $0.042 per million input tokens for d1.2-ultra.

articles.headline: Unlocking Stable On-Policy RL on TPU with Bitwise-Zero Train–Inference Mismatch

This solution addresses floating-point addition errors in separate serving and training paths, using consistent arithmetic operations and standardized reduction orders across TPU meshes.

Public reporting from independent assessments can give the public a clearer view of how labs are evaluating and managing risks. OpenAI has signed agreements with four independent assessors for its first phase of embedded assessments.

articles.headline: Trump Backs Huang Comeback While Nvidia Board Seeks New CEO
articles.blurb: President Trump says he doesn't mind if Jensen Huang were reinstated as Nvidia's CEO. He played down concerns about Huang's relationship with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy, saying that she has yet to be proven to be a spy. Huang has discussed the possibility of returning to his position, and reports say a war room of Silicon Valley executives is being organized to lobby for Huang and get the White House's backing. Nvidia's board is reportedly not considering Huang's return and is searching for a new CEO.

articles.headline: When will humans actually fly on Starship?
articles.blurb: Starship is now rapidly moving toward rapid reusability, but all estimates of human spaceflight on the vehicle should be taken with a gigantic grain of salt. There will be different timelines for humans flying aboard Starship and landing on Earth. The first people to fly on Starship probably won't launch from or land on Earth, as they will probably be NASA's lunar astronauts. Humans will likely not land on Earth in Starship before 2030.

articles.headline: Researchers track whole body movement with just a smartwatch
articles.blurb: EchoMotion is a technology that can track the movement of a person's entire body using ultrasonic sound waves with just an off-the-shelf smartwatch and a lightweight AI model. The system uses the built-in speaker and microphone on a commercial smartwatch to determine a person's body position using a sonar-like sensing system. The technology could potentially be used for tracking workouts, daily activities, and progress on physical rehabilitation. The EchoMotion team is currently developing the technology for use in fitness tracking and exploring the use of the technology in combination with first-person vision on smart glasses to efficiently track the objects that a person handles.

articles.headline: Introducing spatial CSS: A developer preview
articles.blurb: There has been a dramatic rise in the number of websites showing 3D content in the last few years. Spatial web standards should support designing for browsers wherever they run. Safari on visionOS 27.3 comes with a limited feature preview of the proposed spatial CSS API. This article demonstrates how to use the first components of spatial CSS through a case study.

articles.headline: Formal Verification is Not Verifiable
articles.blurb: AI has made formal verification go mainstream. People mean lots of different things when they say something is 'formally verified'. This post attempts to break these down. Formally verified systems can still have bugs, so not all formal verification systems are correct. However, formal verification produces well-defined, reviewable, understandable objects, so it is fairly reliable at finding bugs.

articles.headline: US moves to cut China's remote access to AI chips
articles.blurb: The US Commerce Department is closing a loophole that previously allowed foreign rivals to bypass export restrictions on advanced computer chips by renting access to them from data centers in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil. Companies headquartered in countries deemed to present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion to China, Russia, and Iran must now apply for a license with strict know-your-customer controls when transferring high volumes of advanced chips. Companies with a license must submit monthly reports on transactions that thoroughly detail all parties involved. The rule change will take effect 90 days after it's posted to the Federal Register.

articles.blurb: Staggered scroll animations can use animation-range-start and sibling-index() instead of a custom progress formula. This post contains a worked example that replaces the complicated stagger calculation with one CSS declaration while retaining the browser's built-in easing behavior.

articles.headline: Squircles
articles.blurb: Squircles that look similar can have very different curvature, and Figma's approximation contains discontinuities where its curves join. This article contains an interactive comparison that explains the tradeoffs between Apple, Figma, clothoid, and superellipse shapes, along with the CSS for approximating Apple's corners using corner-shape.

articles.headline: From Skiplists to B+ Trees: Making Valkey Sorted Sets More Memory Efficient
articles.blurb: Valkey 9.2 replaces large sorted sets' skiplist index with a B+ tree that packs entries together and uses SIMD-assisted searches. In a five-million-member test, per-member index overhead fell by 36% to 43%, while command behavior stayed the same. The release is still in candidate testing.

articles.headline: From Tasks to Goals
articles.blurb: Giving an agent an ongoing goal means delegating decisions about which tasks to do and when to act. That requires tool boundaries, feedback, persistent memory, and ways to ask questions, plus stopping rules that let the agent do nothing when no action is useful.

articles.headline: How Rust Changed Me as a Developer
articles.blurb: Rust's enums make variants explicit and let the compiler enforce that every case is handled. This essay explores how sum types and static dispatch change abstraction choices, including when a straightforward enum is more useful than designing an interface.

articles.headline: BrowserPod 4.0
articles.blurb: BrowserPod runs a Linux-like WebAssembly microVM on the user's device, with tools including Node.js, git, bash, and Rust programs. Version 4.0 makes the CDN-loaded runtime free for commercial and production use without an account, while unrestricted networking is a separate service and self-hosting the runtime requires an enterprise license.

articles.headline: dusk bot (Website)
articles.blurb: dusk bot runs a crew of AI helpers, each with its own chat, computer, and memory, using models or subscriptions you already have. Bots can work in parallel, hand off tasks in group chats, and run scheduled routines locally, on your own server, or through dusk's hosted cloud.

articles.headline: Jolt (Website)
articles.blurb: Jolt is a self-hosted Clojure implementation that compiles through Scheme and can produce a standalone native binary with statically linked C dependencies. It supports persistent collections, native C interop, and OS-thread concurrency, but does not provide general JVM interop.

articles.headline: Golden Board: Teaching Chess Without a Shared Language
articles.blurb: Golden Board packs a visual introduction to chess into a 512 KiB binary message, starting with a bootstrap that teaches the recipient how to decode it. The message includes lessons, exercises, and complete games, while its LLM trials explore ambiguities rather than proving an unknown intelligence would understand it.

articles.headline: BenchProofer: Formally Verified Coding Benchmarks, on Demand
articles.blurb: BenchProofer adds formal specifications, verified reference implementations, and audits to coding benchmarks, with SWE-Proof covering all 500 SWE-Bench Verified tasks. Its audit flagged behavioral differences in 134 test-passing Opus 4.8 patches, but human review found actual bugs in only 21 of 41 sampled flags. The distinction matters because a different implementation can still be a valid fix.

articles.headline: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet for secure agentic payments
articles.blurb: OpenAI is launching ChatGPT Wallet, initially for US ChatGPT Pro users through Dots, letting agents complete purchases without seeing users' actual card details while requiring biometric approval for each transaction. Built with American Express, Mastercard, and Visa, the wallet uses payment tokens that preserve existing card rewards and dispute protections. OpenAI is working with payment processors and fraud providers to help merchants recognize legitimate agent-driven transactions.

articles.headline: Anthropic launches Meetings, Whiteboards, Sheets, Data ahead of IPO
articles.blurb: Claude can now join video calls, answer questions in the meeting chat using information from connected apps, and turn planning discussions into timelines with assigned responsibilities. It can also build spreadsheets from a colleague's work and pull information from multiple platforms into dashboards, written summaries, or videos. Interactive connectors bring Claude into full versions of third-party apps, giving teams access to the assistant inside the software they already use.

articles.headline: Stripe bets Tempo can become the payments-first blockchain for stablecoins
articles.blurb: Stripe-backed Tempo is positioning itself as blockchain infrastructure built specifically for payments, reserving most block space for simple money movement so low-margin transactions are not crowded out by higher-value trading activity. The network is targeting cross-border payments, payroll, marketplace payouts, and emerging agentic commerce, with Stripe's Bridge and Privy acquisitions providing stablecoin and wallet infrastructure around the chain.

He breaks down how Revolut built a profitable business around subscriptions and transactions and uses retention and gross profit benchmarks from past launches to decide which new products to scale. He also explains how the company is using AI to shorten compliance reviews that have taken 210 days.

articles.headline: Stock tokens are where stablecoins were in 2023
articles.blurb: Tokenized stocks and ETFs total about $3.2 billion in distributed tokens, roughly 0.004% of the market, against about $431.6 billion in real-world assets onchain per RWA.xyz. Fintech Brainfood author Simon Taylor argues the field splits into four models, from wrapped tokens with no shareholder rights to natively issued stock, and notes 56 of 62 companies opted out of the OKX and ICE pooled offering.

articles.headline: Google connects Wallet to Gemini for personalized finance insights
articles.blurb: Google is rolling out Google Wallet integration to Gemini users in the US, letting the assistant analyze spending, find recurring subscriptions, and help build personalized budgets using transaction data. Users can also link bank and credit card accounts through Plaid for deeper insights, while Gemini remains read-only and cannot move, manage, or invest money.

articles.headline: 8 questions for the Wells Fargo wealth unit's AI chief
articles.blurb: Wells Fargo's AI Teammate assistant has logged hundreds of thousands of interactions since launching last quarter, according to wealth and investment management AI head Andre Mansour, who joined from Google six months ago. Mansour reports the tool runs as an agent over Advisor Gateway's 200-plus adviser tools, cuts meeting prep from hours to a couple of prompts, and expects advisers to become an approval layer for clients' own AI agents.

articles.headline: Jane Street more than doubled its Nvidia stake in Q3 filings
articles.blurb: Jane Street disclosed 23.8 million Nvidia shares worth about $5.4 billion as of September 30, more than double its 11.8 million-share position in Q2, making Nvidia its second-largest reported holding. The filing does not show Jane Street's current exposure or short positions, and its large options book makes the 13F an incomplete picture of whether the firm was making a directional bet on Nvidia.

articles.headline: Everything is fake
articles.blurb: An FBI-uncovered North Korean operation called FaceStealer stole more than $400 million in crypto over about 18 months using AI-generated impersonations of colleagues on video calls. The same playbook could hit banks, from urgent client transfers to account recovery with a matching face and voice, so biometrics and video confirmation can no longer stand alone. The FBI figures arrive secondhand, via press reports, and the bank scenarios are Skinner's sketch rather than documented cases.

articles.headline: PayPal wants a bank to expand merchant lending and diversify funding
articles.blurb: PayPal says an industrial bank charter would support more lending to its merchant base while giving the company a cheaper and more diversified source of capital, including potential deposits. The move fits PayPal's broader push into financial services across BNPL, Venmo, and merchant credit, while management still intends to keep the overall business relatively balance-sheet light by selectively holding or selling loan assets.

articles.headline: Attackers Used Optimizely to A/B Test Malware on Top Websites
articles.blurb: At least 178 top web destinations unwittingly served a variety of malware exploits against visitors over the past 24 hours thanks to a security vulnerability involving Optimizely, a company that helps websites customize user experiences and test out new features. Experts say the incident, which saw data-stealing malicious software silently injected into sites like the BBC, CNN, Equifax, Ledger and Zoom, was exacerbated by the reality that few popular websites enforce strict rules on the sources of third-party content.

articles.headline: Who Runs the Ransomware Group Qilin?
articles.blurb: The cybercrime group Qilin has emerged as the world's most active ransomware affiliate program, claiming at least 365 victim organizations in the past three months alone. But even top Russian hackers make operational security mistakes, and the administrator of Qilin has made a few key missteps over the last decade that all point to a 36-year-old man living in St. Petersburg, Russia.

articles.headline: Microsoft Fixes Nearly 1,100 Security Vulnerabilities
articles.blurb: Microsoft did another four-digit patch drop today, releasing updates to fix almost 1,100 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and supported software. This month's Patch Tuesday addresses 63 critical flaws -- including a zero-day in Microsoft Outlook -- and comes amid important security updates from other software makers, including Adobe, Apple, Google and Mozilla.

articles.headline: Want to Rent an Internet Address at the White House?
articles.blurb: Several staffers at the White House are using computers or mobile devices equipped with residential proxy services that render their internet address available for others to rent, security experts warned today. One of the proxy services is a Russian company whose founder's web hosting business was ground zero for cyberattacks against election systems in Arizona and Illinois in 2016.
